pooled.note: Observed = distinct stocked products per invoice; simulated = distinct items per visit. 14,707 of 19,646 invoices hold at least one of the 72 products placed in the shop; the rest are left out.

Observed = one unit of each stocked product on an invoice, at the shop's calibrated prices; simulated = one unit of each item a visit bought. 14,707 of 19,646 invoices hold at least one of the 72 products placed in the shop; the rest are left out.

Whole baskets: 14,707 invoices holding at least one of the 72 products placed in the shop against 1,793 simulated visits that bought one, each reduced to its purchases of those products per category (9 categories; 67,682 reference and 8,282 simulated purchases). Statistic = Pearson chi-square of the 2 x K table of category totals; p from 2,000 random reassignments of the visit / invoice labels (seed 20260924), which move each basket whole. Naive item-level p = 0.865 (the chi-square(8) tail, which treats every purchase as independent; the reassigned statistics average 1.54 x its null mean). Effect size: the category shares differ by a total-variation distance of 0.010 (Cramer's V = 0.007 at a 11% simulated share of the purchases, 0.012 balanced; V shrinks as the split grows uneven, so it is not read against conventional benchmarks).

Informational, a test of the data rather than the simulator: the dataset's same-day inter-arrival gaps, each divided by the local mean gap the calibrated hour-of-day rate implies (the rate integrated over the gap), against a Poisson reference at the same hourly rates over the same number of trading days. Null: non-homogeneous Poisson process whose rate follows the calibrated hour-of-day profile and is the same on every trading day (the live simulator's arrival law); under it the rescaled gaps are Exp(1). Both sides are stamped at the source's 60 s resolution before rescaling. Rescaled data: mean 0.922, coefficient of variation 1.204 (Exp(1): 1 and 1); a CV above 1 points to a rate that varies between days or to bursts, which the null leaves out.
pooled.null: non-homogeneous Poisson process whose rate follows the calibrated hour-of-day profile and is the same on every trading day (the live simulator's arrival law)

Whole baskets: 14,707 invoices holding at least one of the 72 products placed in the shop against 360 simulated visits that bought one, each reduced to its purchases of those products per category (9 categories; 67,682 reference and 1,643 simulated purchases). Statistic = Pearson chi-square of the 2 x K table of category totals; p from 2,000 random reassignments of the visit / invoice labels (seed 20260924), which move each basket whole. Naive item-level p = 0.0951 (the chi-square(8) tail, which treats every purchase as independent; the reassigned statistics average 1.51 x its null mean). Effect size: the category shares differ by a total-variation distance of 0.035 (Cramer's V = 0.014 at a 2% simulated share of the purchases, 0.046 balanced; V shrinks as the split grows uneven, so it is not read against conventional benchmarks).

Informational, a test of the data rather than the simulator: the dataset's same-day inter-arrival gaps, each divided by the local mean gap the calibrated hour-of-day rate implies (the rate integrated over the gap), against a Poisson reference at the same hourly rates over the same number of trading days. Null: non-homogeneous Poisson process whose rate follows the calibrated hour-of-day profile and is the same on every trading day (the live simulator's arrival law); under it the rescaled gaps are Exp(1). Both sides are stamped at the source's 60 s resolution before rescaling. Rescaled data: mean 0.922, coefficient of variation 1.204 (Exp(1): 1 and 1); a CV above 1 points to a rate that varies between days or to bursts, which the null leaves out.

list_chain.test: Drawn lists vs reference invoices
list_chain.note: Every cohort visit's drawn list (the stocked invoice it took at spawn, paying or not) against the reference invoices holding a placed product, per category, whole baskets relabelled.

list_chain.test: Drawn lists, paying vs unpaid visits
list_chain.note: The drawn lists of the 16 cohort visits that did not pay against those of the 360 that did, per category, whole baskets relabelled: which drawn invoices end as paid visits. Disjoint samples; the unpaid side is small, so the test has little power and a pass is not evidence of no selection.

completion.note: within-visit, so described rather than tested: the paying visits' drawn and bought category shares
